html:
Pieter Bruegel the Elder was a Flemish painter who worked in Antwerp and Brussels in the 1550s and 1560s. He is famous for his scenes of peasant life and landscape.

His paintings show village weddings and dances, harvest work, children's games and Flemish proverbs, crowded with people. The Hunters in the Snow and the other paintings of the seasons are among the first great landscapes in European art. The Tower of Babel and The Triumph of Death show his darker side.

He painted in the years when the Low Countries were sliding into the revolt against Spain, the Eighty Years' War, and some see hidden comments on Spanish rule in his work. His sons and grandsons carried on as painters. He followed Jan van Eyck in Flemish realism and worked in the boom city of Antwerp. See Belgium.
